description: Choose backend architecture for internal analytics service. Team of 4. No dedicated DevOps. 3-week deadline. $200/month budget cap.

constraints.label: Infrastructure Budget <= $200/month
constraints.description: Monthly infrastructure cost must remain under $200 USD.

constraints.label: Team Can Deliver Without New Learning Curve
constraints.description: The team must be able to build and maintain this without significant ramp-up time.

constraints.label: Deliverable Within 3 Weeks
constraints.description: First working version must be deployed within 3 weeks.

constraints.label: p95 Response Time < 200ms
constraints.description: Dashboard queries must return in under 200ms at p95 under moderate load.

constraints.label: Operable Without Dedicated DevOps
constraints.description: The team has no dedicated DevOps. Infrastructure must be manageable by engineers.

constraints.label: No Hard Vendor Lock-in
constraints.description: Architecture should not create dependencies that are costly to undo within 12 months.

capabilities.note: Runs on existing Vercel deployment. No additional infrastructure cost at current scale.
Team already builds in Next.js daily. Zero ramp-up required.
API routes can be added to existing codebase immediately. No new service setup.
Adequate at current scale. Cold starts on Vercel Functions may cause p95 spikes under initial load.
Managed deployment via Vercel. No server management required.
Vercel has some lock-in characteristics, but API routes are standard. Migration to separate service is feasible.
Requires a persistent server. Estimated $20-40/month. Within budget but adds a new cost line.
Team knows Node.js but has not run a separate service before. Setup will add 3-5 days of learning.
New service, new deployment, new CI configuration. Feasible in 3 weeks but leaves little margin.
Persistent Node.js process eliminates cold starts. Fastify is well-suited to high-throughput query APIs.
Manageable on Railway or Render, but adds a second deployment target to monitor.
Standard Node.js with no proprietary APIs. Fully portable.
Serverless pricing at this scale is effectively free.
Team has minimal serverless experience. AWS configuration, IAM, API Gateway all require significant learning.
Setting up production-ready Lambda from scratch would likely exceed 3 weeks.
Cold starts are a real risk. Provisioned concurrency mitigates but adds cost.
AWS configuration surface area is large. Without DevOps, ongoing maintenance burden.
AWS Lambda creates meaningful vendor dependency. Migration is feasible but non-trivial.
